## What an execution rate needs

Two numbers for the same jurisdiction and fiscal year: the original allocation, and the realised
spend. They come from different documents and the second is published later, which is the whole
difficulty.

- Allocation: the development programme table in the jurisdiction's white paper. Punjab
  FY2022-23 is at the White Paper on the Budget 2022-23 - Government of Punjab (p. 74 of the file, printed page 2-21), Table 2.1: Annual Development Programme (Punjab).
- Realised: either the revised estimate column in the *following* year's white paper, or the
  quarterly fiscal operations statement. The federal development line for comparison is at
  the Consolidated Federal and Provincial Fiscal Operations 2022-23 (Q3) (p. 8 of the file, printed page 7), Table 1.3: Development Expenditure.

## Coverage

| Jurisdiction | Allocation series | Realised series | Usable |
|---|---|---|---|
| Punjab | Complete | Complete | Yes |
| Sindh | Complete | Complete | Yes |
| Khyber Pakhtunkhwa | Complete | Two years missing | Mostly |
| Balochistan | Two gaps | Sparse | Marginal |
| Azad Jammu and Kashmir | Sparse | Not published in this form | No |
| Gilgit-Baltistan | Sparse | Not published in this form | No |

The last two rows are the reason the headline number in the draft covers four jurisdictions and not

# Provincial ADP Execution — Working Folder

This folder holds the work on provincial development spending execution rates.

## Layout

- `01_inputs/` — the extracted budget tables, one CSV per jurisdiction and fiscal year
- `02_scripts/` — the cleaning and reshaping scripts, run them in numerical order
- `03_intermediate/` — the reshaped long-format panel before the execution ratios are computed
- `04_figures/` — the charts for the draft

Run `02_scripts/01_load_inputs.R` first, then `02_reshape_panel.R`, then `03_execution_ratios.R`.
The panel that everything else depends on is written to `03_intermediate/adp_panel_long.csv`.

If the ratios look wrong for Balochistan it is almost always because the revised estimate column
is missing for that year and the script silently falls back to the budget estimate. There is a
check for this at the bottom of `03_execution_ratios.R` but it only warns, it does not stop.

## Known issues

- The AJK figures before FY2015-16 are in a different unit and are not rescaled anywhere yet.
- Two of the KP white papers have the ADP table split across a page break and the second half
  was dropped in the first extraction pass. Both were re-done by hand.

Four copies on disk, and the one with the newest modification date is *not* the current one.

## Which is current

**`RA Work/adp_execution/clean/prov_sindh_adp_series.csv`** — vintage `prov_sindh_adp::v4`, source `economic_survey_2026`, covering 2010-11 → 2025-26.

The tiebreaker is the `vintage_label`/`source_doc` columns, not file timestamps:

| File | Vintage | Source doc | Ends | mtime |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `RA Work/adp_execution/clean/…_series.csv` | **v4** | economic_survey_2026 | 2025-26 | 2021-12-17 |
| `.old_backup/provincial_fiscal_panel/clean/…_wrong_year_in_header.csv` | v2 | economic_survey_2022 | 2020-21 | 2020-11-06 |
| `archive/2024 cleanup/federal/…_series.csv` | v1 | fiscal_operations_2020 | 2019-20 | **2023-11-25** |
| `Conferences/NEUDC 2019/…_series.csv` | v0 | economic_survey_2017 | 2016-17 | 2018-01-24 |

The archive copy is the trap — newest mtime, second-oldest vintage. The v4 file is also what feeds `RA Work/adp_execution/clean/adp_execution_panel.csv` (identical 16 rows), which is the corroborating signal that it's the live one.

## What v4 says for 2025-26

**Rs 383 billion**, `obs_status = P` (provisional/budgeted, not outturn). Context from the tail of the series:

- 2023-24: 298.0 (F, final)
- 2024-25: 334.0 (R, revised)
- 2025-26: 383.0 (P)

So it's a budget figure, not a realised one — per your own memo's trap #1, the revised estimate gets revised again, so cite it as `economic_survey_2026` and expect it to move.

## Two things to check before you use it

**v4 is on a different level from every earlier vintage.** It isn't just extra years — the overlapping years are all ~14.5% lower, remarkably uniformly:

| FY | v0/v1/v2 | v4 | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2010-11 | 61.7 | 53.0 | 0.859 |
| 2015-16 | 111.7 | 95.0 | 0.850 |
| 2017-18 | 129.7 | 111.0 | 0.856 |
| 2020-21 | 174.2 | 148.0 | 0.850 |

A near-constant scaling like that reads as a coverage or definitional change (district ADP or foreign project assistance moving in or out of the headline), not noise. **Do not splice v4 onto pre-2021 numbers from the older files** until you've confirmed what changed against the source table. v4 is also rounded to whole billions where the older vintages carry a decimal.

**The `.old_backup` v2 copy has a genuine bug matching its filename:** its last two rows are both labelled `2020-21` (148.0 R and 194.6 P). The second is almost certainly 2021-22. Only matters if anything still reads that path.

Two side notes: `Sources/Provincial/Sindh/White Papers/2025-26/` has the primary white paper, but I couldn't open it here — no poppler installed, so I couldn't independently verify the 383 against the source table. And `RA Work/adp_execution/README.md` describes a folder layout (`01_inputs/`, `02_scripts/`, `03_intermediate/`) that no longer exists — the actual dirs are `raw/`, `scripts/`, `clean/`, and the script it says to run first isn't there.
